title: Approved pull-request bot identities
description: The allowlist scripts/check-issue-link and scripts/check-dco consult (through the one shared derivation, scripts/pr_bot_identity.py) to exempt a pull request's range from the issue-link and DCO sign-off trailers (req-cicd-issue-link-6, req-cicd-dco-signoff-2). An entry is an identity, not a name: the numeric GitHub account id and the account type recorded on the entry (Bot for a GitHub App, User for a declared machine user) authorize together; the login is diagnostics. The file is read by a stdlib-only host tool (shape-checked at load, fail-closed) and validated against this schema by tap/tests/test_check_issue_link.py.

description.description: Why this file exists and what is deliberately absent from it.

approved.description: Deliberately approved bot identities (GitHub Apps, or declared machine users). Order is irrelevant; ids are unique.

login.description: The account login as GitHub reports it, for diagnostics and audit. Never used for authorization. A Bot login ends in [bot]; a User login does not (enforced below).

id.description: GitHub's numeric account id (github.event.pull_request.user.id) — the authorizing identity. Taken from GitHub's /users/<login> response, never guessed.

type.description: GitHub account type as /users/<login> reports it; the authenticated pull-request author's type must EQUAL it. Bot is a GitHub App. User is allowed only for a declared machine user with no role on this repository (the org-bots fork bot), and its note must say so; a human's account is never listed.

verified.description: The date the id/type/login triple was read from GitHub.

note.description: Which system this identity is and why it is approved.
